The test image shows a soybean field with scattered browning/yellowing of leaves and some wilted/dead plant tissue mixed among green plants. Key observations:
- Field-level view, whole plants affected
- Patchy distribution of brown/tan dead leaves throughout the canopy
- Stems appear to still be standing (not lodged)
- Green and brown/tan areas intermixed

Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome, Brown_Stem_Rot, Phytophthora, White_Mold. Let me view reference images.
The SDS reference top-left image looks very similar to the test image — a field with scattered yellowing/browning leaves while stems remain upright. Let me check a few more candidates to confirm.
None of those match as well as SDS. Let me view a few more to be thorough.

Now I have enough evidence to make my determination.

**Analysis:**
- **Test image**: Field-level view of soybean showing scattered brown/tan dead leaves mixed among green plants. Plants remain upright with wilted/dead foliage. Classic mid-season epidemic pattern.
- **SDS reference** (top-left panel): Near-identical field view — yellowing/browning leaves while stems stand, same row pattern and color distribution. The SDS collage also shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis on close-up leaves and the characteristic root/stem crown symptoms.
- **Charcoal_Rot** field view is similar but shows more complete, premature drying of entire plants along rows, not the mixed green/brown pattern seen.
- **Septoria** shows more uniform yellowing across lower canopy.
- **Phytophthora**, **White_Mold**, **Anthracnose**, **Soybean_rust** — all inconsistent with the field-level pattern.

The key distinguishing feature is the characteristic SDS field pattern: leaves turning yellow then necrotic (interveinal chlorosis/necrosis) while stems remain green and upright, creating a patchy brown-and-green field appearance mid-season.
